tell: Very tall slim concrete poles carrying dense bundles of wire, everywhere including cities.
detail: Japan never buried its cables. Streets are strung with heavy wire bundles on thin round concrete poles, often with a transformer drum near the top and vertical address plates fixed to the shaft.

tell: Thick untreated wooden poles with a single horizontal crossarm.
detail: North America runs on wood. Poles are heavy, dark-stained timber, often with a transformer can bolted partway up and a streetlight on a curved arm.

tell: Square-section concrete poles with a flat face, usually leaning slightly.
detail: Brazil's poles are cast concrete with a rectangular cross-section rather than round, which reads as a flat grey slab from the road. Very common across the whole country.

tell: Tapered round concrete poles, frequently painted at the base, with messy wire bundles.
detail: Indonesian poles narrow noticeably towards the top and carry chaotic tangles of low-voltage and telecom cable. Combine with left-hand traffic and Indonesian-language signs.

tell: Square concrete poles with regularly spaced holes down the shaft.
detail: Thai concrete poles are cast with a row of circular voids through the shaft, a detail you can spot at distance once you know to look. Left-hand traffic and Thai script confirm.

tell: Grey concrete poles, often with a wooden top section spliced on.
detail: A very common Russian and post-Soviet pattern is a concrete base pole with a timber upper section bolted to it, which looks like two different poles joined halfway up.

tell: A-frame concrete poles, two legs meeting near the top.
detail: Poland uses a distinctive twin-leg concrete pole that forms a narrow A shape. It stands out sharply from the single-shaft poles used in most of Europe.

tell: Round concrete poles with extremely heavy cable bundles and many crossarms.
detail: Philippine urban poles carry some of the densest visible cabling anywhere, with several stacked crossarms. English-language signage and jeepneys on the road confirm the country.
